subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Sitcom's Three-Camera Origins
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Sitcom's Three-Camera Origins usable.

hook.text: I Love Lucy needed to film live but also create reruns. The solution was three cameras running simultaneously.

buildup.text: Each camera captured a different angle. An editor could cut between them to create a polished show from a live taping.

discovery.text: The three-camera setup became the standard for sitcoms. Friends, Seinfeld, and Big Bang Theory all used it.

twist.text: The format requires a studio audience and a laugh track.

climax.text: Three-camera sitcoms feel stagey by modern standards, but for 50 years they were the backbone of television comedy.

punchline.text: One innovation in 1951 defined comedy for half a century.

quiz.question: Which show pioneered the three-camera sitcom format?
